declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from exchanged proposals addressing both class relief and attorneys’ fees and expenses. Fees were discussed alongside class relief, not deferred until after class relief had been agreed. The fee amount was resolved while the amount of class relief remained under negotiation. This statement does not disclose confidential intermediate offers or counsel’s privileged litigation assessment.

The settlement provides a $27 million class fund and a separate $4 million payment for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any requested fees not awarded will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline. These protections preserve judicial scrutiny of counsel’s compensation and ensure that any fee reduction benefits the class.

Payments will be distributed automatically using Brightline’s existing membership and payment records, without requiring claim forms. Brightline will supply those records without charging the class fund. Reasonable notice and administration expenses will be paid from the class fund, must be documented and court-approved, and are subject to the agreed requirement for a budget before execution. No residual class funds will revert to Brightline; unsuccessful payments will be addressed through a court-approved redistribution procedure.

The $27 million class fund represents approximately 42.2% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges before notice and administration expenses. Although the claims survived dismissal, class certification remains unresolved, recovery on the merits is uncertain, and trial is approximately two to three years away. The settlement provides substantial monetary relief without the risks and delay of continued litigation. Automatic distribution materially strengthens the effectiveness of that relief by eliminating a claims-filing barrier.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate to the class and requests preliminary approval and authorization of appropriate class notice. That assessment rests on the class recovery, litigation risks, distribution safeguards, and independent review of fees—not on the firm’s interest in obtaining compensation. The motion and supporting materials should provide the proposed allocation methodology, administration budget, notice plan, and other information necessary for the Court to evaluate equitable treatment of class members and the requirements of Rule 23(e). Final approval and any fee award remain subject to the Court’s independent review and class members’ opportunity to object.
